name: Glean
tagline: Enterprise "Work AI" platform — permission-aware search across 100+ systems, an AI assistant and a no-code agent builder, all grounded in one Knowledge Graph. $7.2B valuation, June 2025.
verdict: Glean is the search-first entry in this index's agent-platforms category — its Knowledge Graph and permission-aware indexing across 100+ workplace systems come before agent-building, not after, which is a genuinely different foundation from Moveworks' ticket-resolution focus, n8n/Dify's workflow-canvas approach, or Lindy/Relevance AI's consumer-facing no-code builders. That foundation is backed by real scale: a $7.2B valuation (June 2025), over $765M raised across six rounds, $100M in annual recurring revenue by February 2025, and Fortune-500-grade customers (Booking.com, Zillow, Ericsson) each running thousands of internally-built agents. It also ships MCP support in both directions today — a shipped capability Moveworks' own blog admits is still just "planned." The honest catches: Glean publishes no price list at all (Vendr's buyer-data aggregation puts the median deal at $98,890/year across 174 tracked purchases, with typical enterprise minimums around 100–250 seats), G2 reviewers flag it as genuinely expensive with a mandatory support fee near 10% of contract value on top, and its chat still produces occasional hallucinations like any LLM-backed assistant. Pick Glean if your agent strategy starts with "can it find and reason over everything we already know" rather than "can it automate this one workflow"; look at Dify or n8n instead if you want self-hosted, budget-transparent workflow automation, or Moveworks if IT/HR ticket deflection specifically is the job.
